Capstone Project Assignment | aiQuest Intelligence
Overview
The Capstone Project is the culminating assessment of the Generative & Agentic AI course. It 
requires you to independently design, build, and present a functional AI agent or AI-powered 
system that demonstrates your mastery of the concepts, tools, and techniques covered 
throughout the course.
Choose ONE project from the eight options below, or propose a similar project of your own 
(subject to instructor approval). Each project has defined requirements, but you are encouraged 
to add your own creative enhancements. Your project should reflect real-world applicability and 
technical depth.
General Guidelines
• Scope: You may work individually or in a team of up to 2 members.
• Timeline: 2 weeks from assignment date. Final submission and presentation on the last 
class (Class 12).
• Code Quality: Clean, well-commented code with a clear project structure. Include a 
README with setup and run instructions.
• Presentation: 5-7 minute presentation and walkthrough. Live demo is optional but 
encouraged. Be prepared for Q&A from the instructor and peers.

Project Options
Choose ONE of the following eight projects, or propose a similar project of your own.
Project 1: Research & Summarization Agent
Build an autonomous AI agent that can accept a research topic, search the web or a document 
corpus for relevant information, synthesize findings, and produce a well-structured summary 
report. The agent should demonstrate reasoning, source evaluation, and iterative refinement.
Learning Objectives
• Understand autonomous agent architecture (planning, execution, reflection)
• Implement web search and document retrieval as agent tools
• Apply prompt engineering for structured content generation
• Practice information filtering and quality evaluation
Suggested Tech Stack
Python, LangChain/CrewAI, OpenAI/Hugging Face API, SerpAPI or Tavily for web search, Streamlit 
for UI
Required Features
1 Accept a research topic or question from the user
2 Search multiple sources (web, uploaded documents, or APIs)
3 Filter, rank, and deduplicate information by relevance
4 Generate a structured report with sections: Introduction, Key Findings, Analysis, Conclusion
5 Include source citations and references
6 Support iterative refinement (user can ask follow-up questions)
Deliverables
✓ Complete source code with README and setup instructions
✓ Working demo (Streamlit app or CLI) - optional but encouraged
✓ Sample output report on a chosen topic
✓ Short presentation (5-7 minutes) explaining architecture and decisions

Project 2: Data Analysis & Visualization Agent
Create an AI-powered agent that accepts a dataset (CSV/Excel), understands its structure 
through automated exploration, performs statistical analysis, and generates meaningful 
visualizations with natural language explanations. The agent should turn raw data into 
actionable insights.
Learning Objectives
• Build agents that interact with structured data programmatically
• Integrate code execution (Python/Pandas) as an agent tool
• Generate dynamic visualizations driven by LLM reasoning
• Practice safe code execution and error handling in agent pipelines
Suggested Tech Stack
Python, LangChain (with PythonREPL tool), Pandas, Matplotlib/Plotly, OpenAI API, Streamlit or 
FastAPI
Required Features
1 Upload and auto-detect dataset structure (columns, types, missing values)
2 Perform exploratory data analysis (EDA) automatically
3 Answer natural language questions about the data (e.g., 'What is the average sales by region?')
4 Generate charts and visualizations based on user queries
5 Provide written insights and explanations alongside each visualization
6 Handle errors gracefully when data is malformed or queries are ambiguous
Deliverables
✓ Complete source code with README and setup instructions
✓ Working demo with at least 2 sample datasets (optional but encouraged)
✓ Screenshots or exported charts from sample analysis
✓ Short presentation (5-7 minutes) explaining architecture and approach

Project 3: Personal AI Assistant with Memory
Develop a conversational AI assistant that remembers user preferences, past conversations, 
and context across sessions. The assistant should provide personalized responses, manage 
tasks, and demonstrate both short-term and long-term memory capabilities.
Learning Objectives
• Implement different types of memory (buffer, summary, vector-based)
• Design persistent storage for long-term user context
• Apply LangChain memory modules in a real application
• Understand the balance between context window limits and memory retrieval
Suggested Tech Stack
Python, LangChain (ConversationBufferMemory, VectorStoreMemory), ChromaDB/FAISS, OpenAI 
API, Streamlit
Required Features
1 Conversational interface with natural dialogue flow
2 Short-term memory: remember context within a single session
3 Long-term memory: persist user preferences and facts across sessions
4 Personalized responses based on stored user profile and history
5 Ability to recall and reference past conversations when relevant
6 Task management features (set reminders, save notes, track to-dos)
Deliverables
✓ Complete source code with README and setup instructions
✓ Working demo showing multi-session memory persistence (optional but encouraged)
✓ Example conversation logs demonstrating personalization
✓ Short presentation (5-7 minutes) explaining memory architecture

Project 4: Multi-Agent Chat System
Build a system where multiple AI agents with distinct roles (e.g., Researcher, Analyst, Writer, 
Critic) collaborate to accomplish complex tasks. Agents should communicate, delegate 
subtasks, and produce a unified output through structured collaboration.
Learning Objectives
• Understand multi-agent orchestration and communication patterns
• Implement role-based agent design using CrewAI
• Design effective agent workflows with planning and feedback loops
• Practice task decomposition and delegation strategies
Suggested Tech Stack
Python, CrewAI/AutoGen, OpenAI API, Streamlit for monitoring UI
Required Features
1 Define at least 3 distinct agent roles with clear responsibilities
2 Implement structured communication between agents
3 Support task decomposition: break complex tasks into subtasks
4 Include a planning/orchestration agent that coordinates workflow
5 Implement a feedback/critic agent that reviews and improves outputs
6 Display agent communication logs and decision traces
Deliverables
✓ Complete source code with README and setup instructions
✓ Working demo with at least 2 different task scenarios (optional but encouraged)
✓ Agent interaction diagram showing communication flow
✓ Short presentation (5-7 minutes) explaining multi-agent architecture

Project 5: Auto-Document Reader (RAG-Powered)
Create an intelligent document Q&A system using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). 
Users upload documents (PDFs, text files, or web pages), and the system indexes them, 
retrieves relevant passages, and generates accurate answers grounded in the source material.
Learning Objectives
• Implement a complete RAG pipeline from document ingestion to response generation
• Practice document chunking, embedding, and vector storage strategies
• Evaluate retrieval quality and answer faithfulness
• Handle multiple document formats and large document collections
Suggested Tech Stack
Python, LangChain/LlamaIndex, ChromaDB/Pinecone, OpenAI Embeddings, PyPDF2/Unstructured, 
Streamlit
Required Features
1 Support multiple document formats (PDF, TXT, DOCX, web URLs)
2 Intelligent document chunking with overlap for context preservation
3 Vector embedding and storage with efficient similarity search
4 Natural language Q&A with source attribution (show which chunks were used)
5 Handle multi-document queries (search across all uploaded documents)
6 Conversation mode: follow-up questions with context awareness
Deliverables
✓ Complete source code with README and setup instructions
✓ Working demo with at least 3 pre-loaded sample documents (optional but encouraged)
✓ Evaluation report comparing different chunking/embedding strategies
✓ Short presentation (5-7 minutes) explaining accuracy and source tracing

Project 6: n8n Automation Workflow (AI-Powered)
Design and build an end-to-end AI-powered automation workflow using n8n that solves a real 
business problem. The workflow should integrate LLM capabilities with external services, 
handle data transformations, and demonstrate practical no-code/low-code agentic AI 
implementation.
Learning Objectives
• Master n8n workflow design: nodes, triggers, routing, and error handling
• Integrate LLM nodes (OpenAI/Anthropic) for intelligent processing
• Connect multiple external services and APIs in a cohesive pipeline
• Understand when to use no-code vs. code-based approaches
Suggested Tech Stack
n8n (self-hosted or cloud), OpenAI/Anthropic API nodes, Google Sheets/Airtable, Email/Slack 
integrations, Webhook triggers
Required Features
1 Multi-step workflow with at least 5 connected nodes
2 LLM integration for content generation, classification, or summarization
3 External service integration (email, spreadsheets, messaging, or databases)
4 Conditional logic and branching based on AI output
5 Error handling and retry mechanisms
6 Scheduled or webhook-triggered execution
Deliverables
✓ Exported n8n workflow JSON file
✓ Step-by-step documentation with screenshots of the workflow
✓ Demo video or live walkthrough showing the workflow in action (optional but encouraged)
✓ Short presentation (5-7 minutes) explaining the business problem and solution

Project 7: Customer Support Chatbot with Escalation
Build an intelligent customer support chatbot that handles common queries using a knowledge 
base, understands customer intent, and seamlessly escalates complex or unresolved issues to 
a human agent. The system should track conversation state and provide context during 
escalation.
Learning Objectives
• Design intent classification and routing logic for support scenarios
• Implement RAG-based knowledge retrieval for FAQ and product information
• Build escalation workflows with context handoff
• Practice conversation state management and sentiment detection
Suggested Tech Stack
Python, LangChain, ChromaDB, OpenAI API, Streamlit/FastAPI, optional: n8n for escalation 
workflow
Required Features
1 Knowledge base integration for answering common questions (FAQ, product info)
2 Intent classification: identify what the customer needs
3 Sentiment analysis: detect frustration or urgency for proactive escalation
4 Multi-turn conversation handling with context preservation
5 Escalation trigger: transfer to human agent with full conversation summary
6 Admin dashboard showing conversation logs, escalation rates, and common topics
Deliverables
✓ Complete source code with README and setup instructions
✓ Working demo with a sample knowledge base (at least 20 FAQ entries) - optional but 
encouraged
✓ Example escalation scenario walkthrough
✓ Short presentation (5-7 minutes) explaining both self-service and escalation flows

Project 8: Content Generation Pipeline
Create a multi-stage AI content generation pipeline that takes a topic or brief as input and 
produces polished, publish-ready content through automated stages of research, outlining, 
drafting, editing, and formatting. The pipeline should demonstrate chained LLM operations with 
quality control.
Learning Objectives
• Design multi-stage LLM pipelines with intermediate quality checks
• Implement chain-of-thought workflows for content creation
• Practice prompt engineering for different content generation stages
• Build self-evaluation and refinement loops
Suggested Tech Stack
Python, LangChain (SequentialChain/LCEL), OpenAI API, optional: CrewAI for multi-agent 
approach, Streamlit
Required Features
1 Accept content brief: topic, target audience, tone, length, and format
2 Research stage: gather relevant information and key points
3 Outline generation with user approval before proceeding
4 Draft generation following the approved outline
5 Automated editing pass: grammar, clarity, consistency, and fact-checking
6 Multiple output formats: blog post, social media thread, newsletter, or report
Deliverables
✓ Complete source code with README and setup instructions
✓ Working demo generating at least 2 different content types (optional but encouraged)
✓ Sample outputs showing each pipeline stage (outline, draft, final)
✓ Short presentation (5-7 minutes) explaining the pipeline architecture and quality control

Submission Guidelines
1. GitHub Repository: Push your complete project to a public or shared GitHub repository. 
Include a detailed README.md with installation steps, usage instructions, and 
architecture overview.
2. Live Demo (Optional): If you choose to include a demo, it can be hosted (Streamlit 
Cloud, Hugging Face Spaces) or run locally during your presentation. Screenshots or 
recorded walkthroughs are acceptable alternatives.
3. Presentation Slides: Prepare 5-10 slides covering: problem statement, architecture, 
results/screenshots, challenges faced, and what you learned.
4. Deadline: All code must be pushed and accessible before Class 12. If you anticipate a 
delay of more than 2 weeks, please inform the instructor in advance.
Tips for Success
• Start early and build incrementally. Get a basic version working first, then add features.
• Use version control (Git) from day one. Commit frequently with meaningful messages.
• Test your project with different inputs and edge cases before your presentation.
• Focus on quality over quantity. A well-built system with 4 solid features beats 8 broken ones.
• Ask questions in the course community if you get stuck. Collaboration on ideas is 
encouraged (but code must be your own).
• Review the course materials from Classes 1-11. Your capstone should demonstrate skills 
from across the entire course.
Good luck and build something amazing!
